blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا نَدْرُسُ بِنْيَةَ الْفِعْلِ؟
Arabic verbs are compact information systems. Recognising their layers makes reading faster and production more accurate.
### Core
Identify roots, past/present forms and the acting person.
### Develop
Classify sound, initial-weak, hollow, final-weak and doubled verbs.
### Stretch
Explain why a visible form changes while the root meaning remains connected.
[callout] Communication target: Given a verb in context, identify its family, person and time frame.
## Diagnostic start
Try the system before the explanation.
## The five layers inside a verb
Start by seeing the system rather than memorising disconnected endings.

TABLE: Layer | Question | Example // Root | What core consonants carry the main meaning? | ك-ت-ب // Pattern/stem | How is the root shaped? | كَتَبَ / يَكْتُبُ // Tense/aspect | Is the action completed or ongoing/habitual? | كَتَبَ / يَكْتُبُ // Person | Who performs the action? | كَتَبْتُ / كَتَبْنَا // Context | What completes the meaning? | كَتَبْتُ رِسَالَةً.
[callout] Key idea: Arabic verbs package several pieces of information into one word. كَتَبْنَا already tells us “we wrote”.
## A map of sound and weak verb families
The labels help you predict what may change, but they do not replace learning actual forms.

TABLE: Family | Arabic term | Signal | Examples // Sound | السَّالِمُ | No weak radical and no doubled final pair | كَتَبَ، دَرَسَ // Initial weak | الْمِثَالُ | و or ي is the first radical | وَصَلَ / يَصِلُ // Hollow | الْأَجْوَفُ | و or ي is the middle radical | قَالَ، زَارَ، قَامَ // Final weak | النَّاقِصُ | و or ي is the final radical | دَعَا، مَشَى، رَمَى // Doubled | الْمُضَعَّفُ | Second and third radicals match | مَرَّ، رَدَّ
[callout] Do not guess from spelling alone. Learn a high-frequency verb as a pair: قَالَ / يَقُولُ , زَارَ / يَزُورُ , مَشَى / يَمْشِي .
## Person, number and gender
A correct verb must match who performs the action.

TABLE: Pronoun | Past with كَتَبَ | Present with يَكْتُبُ // أَنَا | كَتَبْتُ | أَكْتُبُ // أَنْتَ | كَتَبْتَ | تَكْتُبُ // هُوَ | كَتَبَ | يَكْتُبُ // هِيَ | كَتَبَتْ | تَكْتُبُ // نَحْنُ | كَتَبْنَا | نَكْتُبُ
Past tense usually identifies the person mainly through suffixes. Present tense uses the prefix family أ، ت، ي، ن and, for several persons, additional suffixes.
[example] أَنَا كَتَبْتُ أَمْسِ. ⇄ أَنَا أَكْتُبُ الآنَ.
[ar] أَنَا كَتَبْتُ أَمْسِ.
[ar] أَنَا أَكْتُبُ الآنَ.
## How to learn verbs efficiently
Strong retrieval stores connected forms and meaningful use.
### Learn as a four-part entry
قَالَ / يَقُولُ / قَوْلٌ / قُلْ
past · present · verbal noun · useful command, where appropriate
### Learn with a collocation
قَالَ الْحَقِيقَةَ، زَارَ الْمُتْحَفَ، مَرَّ بِالسُّوقِ
The surrounding words protect natural usage and prepositions.
[callout/warning] Scope: This lesson maps the territory. Lesson 2 teaches the actual shape changes in hollow, doubled, initial-weak and final-weak verbs.
## Foundation misconception clinic
A useful correction explains the form, not only the answer.
### The weak letter is not “extra”
✗ قَالَ ← الجذر ق-ل
✓ قَالَ ← الجذر ق-و-ل
The و is a root radical even when it is not visible as و in the past surface form.
### A shadda counts twice
✗ الجذر م-ر
✓ الجذر م-ر-ر
مَرَّ contains two root occurrences of ر.
### Present is not simply “add ي”
✗ ي + كَتَبَ = يَكَتَبَ
✓ كَتَبَ / يَكْتُبُ
The stem vowels may change and must be learned.
### One form is not a full verb entry
✗ قَالَ فقط
✓ قَالَ / يَقُولُ / قَوْلٌ
Connected learning prepares later tense and morphology work.
## Replayable pattern game
Use classification to strengthen later prediction.
## Apply the grammar across skills
Grammar becomes useful when it helps you understand and communicate.
### 📖 Reading workshop
Read a short daily-routine paragraph and circle all verbs. Sort them by past/present and by sound/weak/doubled family.
### 🎧 Listening workshop
A partner reads eight sentences. Record only the verb and identify who acts and whether the action is completed or ongoing.
### 🗣️ Speaking workshop
Give a 45-second answer about what you usually do and what you did yesterday. Use at least four different verbs.
### 🛠️ Editing workshop
Repair a paragraph containing one wrong person ending, one tense mismatch, one guessed weak-verb form and one missing preposition.
### ✍️ Integrated production task
Write 80–100 words introducing your daily routine and one past experience. Underline five verbs and annotate each with its root, time frame and subject.
[callout] Model: أَسْتَيْقِظُ مُبَكِّرًا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ، وَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. أَمْسِ زُرْتُ الْمَكْتَبَةَ وَقَرَأْتُ كِتَابًا.
[callout] Success checklist: Use at least one sound verb, one hollow or weak verb, two different persons and two time frames.
Save and mark complete Clear
Plan the verb changes as a timeline, root map or sentence flowchart. Label each form in Arabic.
Write the paragraph, then create a three-column audit: verb form · root/family · reason it matches the sentence.
## Final mastery check
Check whether you can see the system before studying the detailed changes.
### Lesson mastery summary
- identify the root and main conjugation layers;
- classify common sound, weak and doubled verb families;
- match basic past and present forms to their subjects;
- build a useful multi-form verb entry.
Return in 3–7 days and repeat the final check without reviewing first. Retrieval, not recognition alone, builds secure verb control.
